---
title: "Posterior profiles on multiple criteria"
subtitle: "4.1 · after the postrank vignette m2 and theory book, ch. 12"
description: "Criterion-specific scales, orderings and pairwise direction probabilities for common units."
---

The same sites can rank differently on reading growth and family engagement. The site with the largest posterior
mean on one measure may rank lower on the other.

```{=html}
<div id="app" class="prx-app column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/several-criteria.js"></script>
<script>window.__prxApp = PRX["several-criteria"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("app"));</script>
```

The panels show the posterior means and marginal intervals on their original scales. Lines connect the same
site across the two orders. Selecting a pair gives the probability that the proposed direction is wrong on
each criterion. This comparison can show strong support for opposite directions or weak support on either
measure. The priority order also depends on whether a higher or lower score calls for an earlier visit.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Thirty sites.** There are 397 opposing pairs among 435 pairs. The highest posterior mean belongs to a different
  site on each criterion. Alignment by unit labels displays each unit's criterion-specific profiles.
- **Six sites, B–C.** The error of stating B above C is .007 on score A and .961 on score B. The complete list has
  3 opposing pairs. A very likely direction on one criterion can be very unlikely on another.
- **Six sites, B–D.** The errors are .002 on score A and .760 on score B. The difference remains visible when both panels use the same order of site labels.
- **Reverse score B.** Lower score B now means higher priority. The error of stating B above C on the oriented
  score becomes .039. This change reverses the direction that counts as higher priority without changing the underlying scores.
- **Wider intervals.** The marginal level becomes 95%, while the 397 opposing pairs stay the same. Interval level
  changes the displayed uncertainty bands, not the supplied posterior probabilities or mean orders.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
In the six-site example, score A measures standardized reading growth and score B is a standardized index
of family engagement. Higher scores ordinarily imply earlier visits to document site practices. The example
assigns no funding. Each interval describes one marginal normal posterior. The released marginal summaries for
thirty sites leave the joint draws and the distribution of a composite undetermined.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
pr_tutorial$two$e["B", "C", ]
pr_tutorial$two$e["B", "D", ]
```
